title: A first taste check: titles, dividers and file entries

steps.path: Open Settings; the second picture is the donation dialog
steps.headline: Settings and dialog titles become larger and less heavy.
steps.changed: Both titles move from a small bold label to a slightly larger, medium-weight title. The line underneath stays exactly as it is today.
steps.notice: The title may read more clearly without feeling as heavy as the rows below it.
steps.risk: Long titles may crowd the close button. You'll approve the eventual rule separately.

steps.path: The line below the Settings and dialog titles
steps.headline: Header lines fade before they reach the sides.
steps.changed: The title treatment is identical on both sides; only the line changes. Instead of meeting the outer edges, it begins and ends inside the panel with a soft fade.
steps.notice: The headers may feel less cut into two blocks while still separating the title from the content.
steps.risk: This covers two headers, not structural or content dividers. Those remain separate decisions.

steps.path: Open the file list beside a conversation
steps.headline: Session Files become separate compact cards instead of continuous rows.
steps.changed: Each file now has its own quiet surface and rounded edge. The filename, status and date stay in the same order; no empty thumbnail is added.
steps.notice: It is easier to see where one file ends and another begins, but fewer entries fit at once.
steps.risk: Project Files already has a grid and a list. This choice does not decide that screen or the phone layout.
